title: P300 dataset BI2015b from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: EEG recordings from 44 participants playing Brain Invaders, a visual P300 brain-computer interface game based on an oddball paradigm (Cooperative versus Competitive dataset, BI2015b). Thirty-six aliens are flashed in pseudo-random groups of six symbols. Each participant plays three game sessions with flash durations of 50, 80 and 110 ms. Data were recorded with 32 wet electrodes at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, France, in 2015. A real-time adaptive Riemannian classifier was used, which requires no calibration.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 512 Hz from 32 active wet Ag/AgCl electrodes (g.tec g.USBamp, 10-10 montage) with the reference on the right earlobe and the ground at Fz. Each participant completed three game sessions of 9 levels, one per flash duration (110, 80 and 50 ms). About one minute of resting state and eyes-closed data was recorded before and after the sessions. Events were tagged in hardware through a USB digital-to-analog converter to reduce jitter, and no digital filter was applied. An online adaptive Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean classifier determined the participants' commands.
